findings.description: The lock-window AC ('scan ran without the lock') was underspecified and slightly contradictory: the module destructures withStateFileLock (member-crash-notifications.js:59) and getMemberHealth (:75) at load and _internal (:384) does not expose them, yet the plan said to keep _internal shapes stable AND suggested a wrapped lock seam. Flagged by Claude (Medium), Codex (Medium x2), Copilot (Low, also warned the held-lock fixture risks the 2s LockTimeout + Windows flakiness).
findings.resolution: Rewrote the lock-window AC to require a deterministic call-order assertion via ONE specified mechanism: (preferred) an additive optional args.withStateFileLock seam (default real) with a recording wrapper, or (alternative) monkeypatch-before-require of ../hooks/locks + ../hooks/health. Bare timing claims and real held-lock 2s fixtures are explicitly disallowed. Updated Implementation Strategy, Files-to-Modify, Risk Areas split-export note, and the new-test-file description to match.

findings.description: The candidate-manifest re-read under the brief lock was framed as OPTIONAL, but moving the append to a later phase grows the scan->append window (Phase A computes all candidates before Phase B appends any), so a member that gets /stop-member or /clear-member or resumes during the (now multi-second) scan window could receive a false member-crashed notification — the F-001-class guard the persist-after-append logic protects against. Flagged by Copilot (Medium, make required); Codex independently suggested revalidating final candidates before append.
findings.resolution: Made the per-candidate manifest re-validation under the brief lock REQUIRED: re-read the candidate manifest and re-check the cheap manifest-based guards (#1 role, #2 intentionally-stopped, #3 recoverable, #5 ownership) before appendSystemMailbox; skip if any now fails. getMemberHealth is NOT re-run under the lock (avoids reintroducing per-candidate CIM). Added a dedicated AC, an In-Scope bullet, a Risk-Areas entry, and an Open-Question on re-validation depth.

findings.description: The fail-soft PreToolUse AC did not require the test fixture to satisfy the other PreToolUse gates (esp. an armed listener / listenerState). Without that, the test could pass for the wrong reason — observing the normal arm-first block — rather than proving 'sweep error does not deny the tool'.
findings.resolution: Strengthened the fail-soft AC to require the fixture satisfy lead role + armed listener + no pending review-required mail + a non-.crews-write tool, and to assert an allow/no-deny decision while the injected sweep throws.

findings.description: If the optional US-002 throttle-unification ships, a shared per-lead stamp could let the listener-loop skip its own sweep after the hook backstop already touched the stamp; since lib/listener-loop.js:424,432 only calls deliver('crash-sweep') when its own sweep returns appended>0, the listener might not promptly deliver a crash notice the hook-side sweep appended. Claude separately asked that US-002's optional status be explicit about not gating the bugfix ACs.
findings.resolution: Added a US-002 'does NOT gate the bugfix' callout and a requirement that, IF shipped, US-002 includes a listener-delivery test proving the listener still wakes/drains a hook-appended crash notice (via the next fs.watch wake). Reinforced the deferral recommendation.

findings.description: US-003 (release ceremony) implied but did not spell out the submodule two-commit flow; an autonomous implementer could leave a dirty ai-developer-toolkit submodule in the parent codexu repo.
findings.resolution: US-003 now explicitly: (a) the impl member commits the crews changes (6 version stamps via scripts/bump-version.js, tests/version.test.js, prepended CHANGELOG.md) INSIDE ai-developer-toolkit on its topic branch (no dirty submodule); (b) the LEAD owns the codexu parent-pointer bump + root AGENTS.md active-plugin-versions table after merging the submodule branch.
